title: A merge of tick records silently keeps one side
description:
FOUND 2026-09-23. A local xte run's merged record for njj (closed + the run's notes from epic/xte, blocked_by ha9/qu3 from main) appeared as an UNCOMMITTED change in the main checkout, which never edited it.

CAUSE: tk merge-file, the git merge driver for .tick/issues/*.json, is registered as 'tk merge-file %O %A %B %P' and wrote its result to %P. git reads a driver's result from %A only; %P is the file's logical path. So:
  - the commit kept %A untouched (OURS): every tick record both sides of a merge changed lost the other side's change, with no conflict and no marker;
  - the correct merge was written into the working tree at %P and left unstaged.
Reproduced with plain git and the real tk: one branch closed a tick, the other set its priority; the merge commit carried the close and NOT the priority, and 'git status' showed M .tick/issues/abc.json.

Every reconciler integrate and every refresh merges tick records through this driver, so tracker edits have been dropped at merge time for as long as the driver has existed. merge-activity (the activity-log driver) was already correct.

FIXED: ticks #90 (cb852e91) writes to %A with a test that pins git's contract; the local ~/.local/bin/tk is rebuilt from it; ticfac #37 pins the factory image's tk to it; ticks #91 corrects the published contract (bundle 6.0.0), which described the bug as the rule - that last one was raised by the factory's own pi review of #90.
acceptance_criteria: tk merge-file writes to %A and never to %P, pinned by a test; a real git merge of two sides' changes to one tick record commits both; the local tk and the factory image's tk include the fix; the published contract describes %A
